propositions: Bedrock model ids with canonical version suffixes containing colons (e.g. 'anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0') are silently treated as already provider-qualified and lose an explicitly configured provider parameter.
The bug occurs because _resolve_target checks for ':' in model to detect provider-qualification, but Bedrock versioned ids contain colons in their version suffix not as a provider separator.
Configured provider is not checked first before scanning for inline qualifiers, allowing a model string to override an explicit provider directive.
An unqualified versioned Bedrock id subsequently fails with a misleading error that names a fragment of the model id as an unknown provider instead of the actual misconfiguration.
The fix centralizes qualified/unqualified detection into a single shared function split_provider_qualifier that validates prefix format against a regex pattern rather than colon presence alone.

Explicit provider configuration now takes precedence over inline qualification detection, and conflicting directives raise LLMConfigError at config read time rather than failing silently at call time.
